description:
WHY FACULTY?

We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

 
 

ABOUT THE TEAM

 

Our National Security and AI Safety business unit is dedicated to advancing the responsible development and deployment of AI in support of national security and global stability. From strengthening mission-critical capabilities across national security and intelligence, to working with frontier labs to provide robust AI safety red teaming and evaluation, we work at the frontier of high-stakes, high-impact missions.

We understand that powerful AI systems bring both transformative opportunities and complex risks and we are proud to partner with Government and the biggest tech organisations in the world to ensure AI is not just transformative but is also secure, trustworthy and safe for all.

Because of the nature of the work we do with our Government clients, you may need to be eligible for UK Developed Vetting (DV) and willing to work on site with our clients from time to time.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

 

Join us as a Machine Learning Engineer to deliver bespoke, impactful AI solutions for our diverse clients.

 

You will be instrumental in bringing machine learning out of the lab and into the real world, contributing to scalable software architecture and defining best practices. Working with clients, and cross-functional teams, you'll ensure technical feasibility and timely delivery of high-quality, production-grade ML systems.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

 

- Building and deploying production-grade ML software, tools, and infrastructure.

- Creating reusable, scalable solutions that accelerate the delivery of ML systems.

- Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, and commercial leads to solve critical client challenges.

- Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions to ensure project feasibility and impact.

- Defining and implementing Faculty’s standards for deploying machine learning at scale.

- Acting as a technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex ML concepts for stakeholders.

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 

- You understand the full machine learning lifecycle and have experience operationalising models built with frameworks like Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.

- You possess strong Python skills and solid experience in software engineering best practices.

- You bring hands-on experience with cloud platforms and infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including architecture and security.

- You've worked with container and orchestration tools such at Docker & Kubernetes to build and manage applications at scale

- You are comfortable with core ML concepts, including probability, statistics, and common learning techniques.

- You're an excellent communicator, able to guide technical teams and confidently advise non-technical stakeholders.

- You thrive in a fast-paced environment, and enjoy the autonomy to own scope, solve and delivery solutions

 

OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS

 

1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

2. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes)

3. System Design Interview (90 minutes)

4. Commercial Interview

We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.

A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.

You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.

This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.

In This Role, You Will

- Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

- Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

- Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

- Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

- Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

- Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

- Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

- Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

- Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

- Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

- Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

- Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

- Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

title: Accounting Manager - Dallas, TX
signals: based in cobalt service partners - hq
description:
Cobalt Service Partners (CSP) is building the nation's leading commercial access and security integration platform. Backed by Alpine Investors , a middle-market private equity firm, we grow by acquiring businesses that install, maintain, and repair commercial gates, doors, loading docks, and integrated security systems.

Since launching in late 2023, Cobalt has acquired 22 partner companies and established itself in a highly attractive and fragmented industry. We have done this by partnering with founder-led companies that have spent decades earning trust in their local markets. Our mission is to honor those legacies, enhance operations through disciplined execution, and drive growth through high-frequency M&A. 

The Role

On-Site ·  Dallas, TX

As Accounting Manager, you'll own accounting for a group of our operating companies, covering the monthly close, reporting, controls, payroll oversight, and the annual audit. This is a hands-on role for someone who likes the details and wants real ownership, while working closely with our regional finance team. Our businesses are project-based, so revenue recognition, job costing, and cash management are at the center of the work. You'll also build the processes and lead the team through the changes that come with joining Cobalt.

What You'll Own

• Monthly close. Run a fast, accurate close and flash report. Prepare and review journal entries, accruals, and account reconciliations.

• Project accounting. Own revenue recognition under ASC 606, job costing, and WIP (over/under billings) across active projects.

• Financial reporting. Own the income statement and balance sheet, including deferred revenue, prepaids, fixed assets. Establish and manage cycle counts and inventory accounting. Prepare the monthly financial package and variance analysis, and explain notable swings to leadership.

• Intercompany accounting. Record, reconcile, and settle intercompany activity: record entries, reconcile balances, and coordinate settlements with the Cobalt platform finance team and sister companies.

• Cash forecasting. Build and maintain a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast.

• Controls, audit, and compliance. Maintain and strengthen internal controls. Prepare PBC schedules and answer auditor questions for the annual audit. Keep tax and regulatory filings current with outside advisors.

• Budget and KPIs. Prepare the annual budget and track the KPIs that drive the business.

• Process and systems. Create, document, and maintain standard procedures for close, AP/AR, payroll, and reporting. Replace manual or risky workflows with standardized, automated ones, and support the regional team on ERP implementations and integrations.

• Team and change management. Lead and develop accounting staff, and make sure payroll, AR, and AP are accurate and on time. Guide the team through new systems, policies, and reporting requirements: explain what's changing and why, train people, and make sure new processes stick.

What We're Looking For

• 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, with hands-on ownership of the monthly close.

• Strong command of GAAP, including ASC 606, reconciliations, accruals, and financial reporting.

• Experience with project-based accounting: job costing, WIP, and over/under billings.

• Experience with inventory accounting, including cycle counts, valuation, and reconciling physical counts to the general ledger.

• Experience running close and reporting across multiple entities, branches, or subsidiaries.

• Comfort with accounting systems (our operating companies run tools such as QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, and ServiceTitan) and the ability to learn new ones quickly.

• Strong Excel and modeling skills.

• Self-directed, and able to bring structure to ambiguity.

Preferred: CPA; public accounting background; construction or field-services industry; experience supervising a team.

Why Cobalt

• A high-growth, PE-backed platform where finance is close to the business

title: SAP Developer
description:
This is a remote position.
Position Overview
We are looking for an experienced SAP Developer with strong hands-on expertise in SAP Security and SAP Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, configuring, and maintaining SAP security roles, access controls, authorization objects, and GRC solutions to ensure secure and compliant access across SAP applications.
The role will support enterprise ERP transformation initiatives, security enhancements, access governance, and ongoing production support. The candidate will work closely with functional teams, business stakeholders, internal audit, and compliance teams to implement effective security controls, minimize access risks, and maintain compliance with organizational policies and audit requirements.
Key Responsibilities
SAP Security & Authorization Development

• Design, develop, configure, and maintain SAP security roles, composite roles, derived roles, and authorization profiles.

• Manage user provisioning, role assignments, authorization objects, and access requests across SAP environments.

• Work with SAP authorization concepts, including PFCG, SU24, SU01, SU53, and ST01, to troubleshoot and resolve authorization issues.

• Support SAP ECC and/or SAP S/4HANA security, including SAP Fiori applications, catalogs, groups, and authorization roles, as applicable.

• Perform role modifications, security testing, transport management, and deployment of security changes across development, quality assurance, and production environments.

• Analyze authorization failures and implement appropriate fixes while following change management procedures.

SAP GRC & Access Control

•
Configure, enhance, and support SAP GRC Access Control solutions, including:

• ARA (Access Risk Analysis): Identify and analyze Segregation of Duties (SoD) conflicts, critical access risks, and sensitive permissions.

• ARM (Access Request Management): Manage and configure access request workflows, approvals, and provisioning processes.

• EAM (Emergency Access Management): Administer Firefighter access, controller assignments, usage logs, and review processes.

• BRM (Business Role Management): Support business role definition, role lifecycle management, and governance.

• Maintain and customize SoD rulesets, risk definitions, functions, and mitigation controls.

• Perform access risk analysis, role simulations, and remediation of identified security conflicts.

• Support User Access Reviews (UAR), periodic access certifications, and emergency access reviews.

• Troubleshoot GRC workflow, integration, provisioning, and authorization issues.

Compliance, Audit & Risk Management

• Support SOX-related controls, internal audits, external audits, and compliance assessments where applicable.

• Maintain evidence for access reviews, role approvals, emergency access usage, and security changes.

• Ensure appropriate segregation between business-critical activities and sensitive transactions.

• Identify opportunities to strengthen access governance and reduce security risks.

• Collaborate with auditors and business process owners to resolve findings and implement corrective actions.

Development, Integration & Production Support

• Analyze security requirements and translate them into technical configurations and development specifications.

• Support security integration with connected SAP applications and identity or provisioning systems, where applicable.

• Work with SAP technical and functional teams to resolve access issues affecting business processes such as finance, procurement, inventory, order management, and supply chain.

• Participate in system upgrades, ERP implementations, security testing, cutover activities, and post-go-live stabilization.

• Follow ITSM processes for incident, problem, change, and release management.

• Maintain technical documentation, configuration records, and operational procedures.
